id: P:Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo
summary: Minyak Rongsharwa Tubten Lek Shé Zangpo studied under Patrul Rinpoche, Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.

Mio Kishimoto is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology who studied at the University of Tokyo from ~1971 to 1979. She served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1994–2007) and held a post at Ochanomizu University (~2007–2018).
Mipam Chökyi Jampa studied under Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye.
Miranda Shaw works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Masatoshi Nagatomi, teacher Robert A. F. Thurman, and postdoctoral mentor Bratindra Nath Mukherjee.

Scholar in religious studies, Indology, and philosophy Mircea Eliade studied at the University of Bucharest and University of Calcutta under Surendranath Dasgupta. He taught at Bucharest, École Pratique des Hautes Études, the Sorbonne (~1945–1948), and the University of Chicago (1957).

Mireille Bénisti was a scholar in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology who earned diplomas from the École du Louvre and EPHE. She held posts at the CNRS (1955), Musées Nationaux (1960), and taught at Royal University of Phnom Penh (1962–1963).

Mireille Helffer worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique as Chargé de Recherche (~1968–1993) and at Paris Nanterre University (attested 1985).

Mirella Keller is a Buddhist studies and sinology scholar who studied at Fo Guang University (MA, 2015–2018) and Eötvös Loránd University (PhD, 2019). She became an assistant professor at Dharma Gate Buddhist College in 2025.
Mirella Lingorska works in Indology and linguistics. As attested in 2026, she holds posts at the University of Zurich as a Temporary Teaching Fellow in Hindi and at the University of Tübingen.

Miri Albahari is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned an MA at the University of Otago and a PhD at the University of Calgary (until 2005). She held affiliations with the University of New South Wales and University of Western Australia.

Miriam Levering was a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology who earned her PhD at Harvard University in 1978. She served as Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Tennessee, Knoxville (attested 2007–2010).

Mirjan Damaška studied at the University of Zagreb and completed his PhD at the University of Ljubljana (1960). His career includes posts at the University of Zagreb, the University of Pennsylvania (1972–1976), and Yale University beginning in 1975–1976.
Miron Winslow was an Indology and linguistics scholar who studied at Middlebury College (~1813–1815) and Andover Theological Seminary (~1815–1818). He founded the American Madras Mission in 1836.

Miroslav Marcovich was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Belgrade (~1937–1941). He held teaching posts at Belgrade (1946–1954), the University of Los Andes (1955–1959), and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1969–1989).
Mitashree Srivastava is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed an M.Sc at the University of Allahabad in 2007. She was appointed associate professor at the University of Delhi in 2013.
Mitchell G. Weiss is an Indology scholar who studied as a student of Ludo Rocher. He held a post as professor at the University of Basel.

Mithilesh Chaturvedi is a scholar in Indology and linguistics affiliated with the University of Delhi's Department of Sanskrit (attested 2009), where he is also attested as professor emeritus in 2026.

Mitsuji Fukunaga was a scholar in philosophy, sinology, and religious studies who studied at Kyoto University. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1961–1982), the University of Tokyo (1974–1979), Kansai University (1982–1986), and the University of Kitakyushu (1986–1989).
Mitsukuni Yoshida was a scholar in Japanology and history/archaeology who studied at Kyoto University (~1942–1945). He later held a post at Kyoto University of the Arts.
Mitsutoshi Moriguchi is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University. He also served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1989–1995).
